origin.description: Turn a vector, matrix, data frame, factor, ts, or zoo into a zoo series.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object. A numeric or integer vector, a matrix, a data frame, a factor, a ts, or a zoo series.
Further arguments passed to zoo when the series is created. A plain vector does not accept order.by here; a matrix, data frame, or factor does.

origin.details: The default method builds the index with seq_len(NROW(x)). A matrix, data frame, or factor is passed to zoo, so order.by and frequency can be set. A data frame becomes a matrix. A ts is turned into a zooreg through the same path as as.zooreg.ts. as.zoo on a zooreg drops the frequency attribute and the zooreg class, and leaves the index as it is. Frequency 4 or 12 on a numeric or integer index becomes yearqtr or yearmon when zoo.calendar is true.
origin.value: A zoo object. A ts becomes a zooreg.
origin.example:
x <- as.zoo(c(2, 4, 6))
cat(paste(coredata(x), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")
cat(paste(index(x), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Turn a vector, matrix, data frame, factor, ts, or zoo into a zoo series.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A list or NumPy vector, a 2-d array, a DataFrame or dict, a factor, a Ts, or a Zoo.

arguments.name: frequency
arguments.text: Observations per unit of time. None leaves the series irregular, except a ts, which keeps its own frequency unless this is set.

arguments.name: calendar
arguments.text: When true, frequency 4 or 12 stores the index as yearqtr or yearmon.

arguments.name: order_by
arguments.text: Index. Accepted for a matrix, data frame, or factor. On a plain vector it is an error, matching the default method.

translation.details: A numeric vector uses 1-based positions as an integer index. A matrix stays column-major. A data frame is stacked the same way as.matrix stacks it. A factor keeps its levels and ordered flag. A Ts is built with zooreg. as_zoo on a regular Zoo drops frequency and regular and keeps the index object. xts, tis, timeSeries, fts, coda, and chron raise.
translation.value: A Zoo. regular is true when frequency is set.
translation.example:
from zoo.as_zoo import as_zoo
import numpy as np
x = as_zoo([2, 4, 6])
print(" ".join(str(int(v)) for v in np.asarray(x.data).reshape(-1)))
print(" ".join(str(int(v)) for v in np.asarray(x.index).reshape(-1)))
